1001337.etyen:
Internationalism, based on the widespread distinguishing formation combining Kongo (“Congo”) with the name of the country's capital, Brazzaville. The capital is added to distinguish the country from Kongo-Kinshasa, the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The second element is ultimately from French Brazzaville, formed from the surname Brazza and ville (“city”), and named after the Italian-French explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza. For the further origin of Kongo, see that entry.
Parallel formations include Norwegian Nynorsk Kongo-Brazzaville, Swedish Kongo-Brazzaville, Afrikaans Ko

1004921.etyen:
From kurfyrste (“prince-elector”) + -lig (“adjective-forming suffix”).
The base kurfyrste (“prince-elector”) is modelled after German Kurfürst (“prince-elector”), literally “electoral prince”, from Kur (“election”) + Fürst (“prince”). German Kur in this sense is from Middle High German kur, küre (“choice, election”), from Old High German kuri (“choice”), ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *kuʀi (“choice, decision”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵews- (“to test, taste, choose”). Fürst ultimately continues Proto-Germanic *furistaz (“first, foremost”), from Proto-Indo-European *preh₂- (“before”).
